Missouri Governor's Mansion to Host Tree Lighting Ceremony and Candlelight Tours

November 27, 2026

Jefferson City

Governor Mike Kehoe and Mrs. Claudia Kehoe invite families to join them for a tree lighting ceremony and candlelight tours at the Missouri Governor's Mansion on
 Friday, December 4.
 The traditional tree lighting at 6:00 p.m. will be followed by candlelight tours until 8:00 p.m., where visitors will be able to walk through the decorated first floor of the Governor's Mansion. 
This year’s Mansion Christmas theme is "White Christmas." To help usher in the Christmas season, participants in the Big Brothers Big Sisters of Jefferson City organization will join the First Family as special guests during the tree lighting ceremony.
The candlelight tours will run again 
Monday, December 7
 from 6:00 p.m. to 8:00 p.m. The candlelight tours are free and open to the public. Visitors will enter through the Madison Street gate.
Toys for Tots representatives will also be in attendance during the candlelight tours to accept donations of new, unwrapped toys, or monetary contributions to support Missouri children this holiday season.
"Claudia and I look forward to welcoming Missouri families back to the People's House this Christmas season and sharing the rich history and beauty of the Governor's Mansion," said 
Governor Kehoe
. "We are grateful to the Mansion team for the incredible work they do to create memorable experiences for visitors from across our state."
In addition to the 36-foot Christmas tree on the Mansion lawn, the Mansion team has sourced two Norway Spruce trees to embellish the entryway leading to the Mansion. The 8-foot trees were selected from Pea Ridge Forest, a wholesale tree nursery and Christmas tree farm near Hermann, Missouri.
The Governor's Gardens and the Maus House will also be decorated, with the Governor's Gardens featuring a 28-foot Christmas tree. Santa and Mrs. Claus will greet families at the Maus House (115 Jefferson Street) from 5:00 p.m. to 7:00 p.m. on 
December 8, 10, 15
 and 
17
.
